chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Abu Kahmas, who said:

I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: A man entered the Masjid, so he began (asking) before the laudation upon Allah and the Blessings upon the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family). So Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The servant hastened with his Lord'. Then another one entered, so he prayed and lauded upon Allah Mighty and Majestic, and sent Blessings upon Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family). So Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Ask, you would be Given'.

Then he (peace be upon him) said: 'In the Book of Ali (peace be upon him) is the laudation upon Allah and the Salat upon His Rasool before the asking, and if one of you goes over to the man seeking the need, so he would love it if you were to be saying to him good (words) before you ask him for the need'.
ai.seo_question: What is the proper etiquette for making du'a according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* establishes the theological principle of *adab al-du'a* (etiquette of supplication), linking the ritual structure of prayer to the efficacy of personal requests. It draws a profound parallel between divine protocol—where Allah invites the supplicant to ask after praise—and human social dynamics, where one offers kindness before making a request, thereby grounding spiritual practice in relatable social wisdom.
